[Scene: An agent and a person talk; the conversation grows into a long scroll.]
An AI agent can work with you through a long conversation. It follows the details as the work unfolds.

[Scene: The scroll reaches a frame, then folds into a short note.]
But the model has a limit to how much conversation it can hold at once. When the conversation gets too big, it’s compressed into a summary.

[Scene: The agent reads the note and resumes the task.]
The agent continues from that summary. It can keep working, but it’s now relying on what the summary says.

[Scene: Some details fade away as the note stays visible.]
Anything important that didn’t make it into the summary is gone from the agent’s view. It may forget a decision, a constraint, or why something was done.

[Scene: A person asks the agent questions about earlier work; the agent checks the summary.]
So how can you tell whether a summary is good? Ask the agent questions about the old work. Can it recall the key choices and details? If not, the summary may need to carry more forward.

[Scene: The agent continues, with the checked summary beside it.]
A summary is a bridge across a long session. The better it preserves what matters, the more smoothly the work can continue.
